speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you have been experiencing intense itching and the appearance of red bumps on your thigh and elsewhere. To help me understand your condition better, can you tell me how long these symptoms have been present and if they have appeared in anyone else in your household?

speaker: Patient
text: 47-year-old male. The patient presents with intense itching of his right thigh region for the past few days. He also mentions the recent formation of ‘red bumps’ in the same area. The patient has recently attended a business conference in Miami. He has a past medical history of hypertension, diabetes type 2, and hyperlipidemia. The patient’s medication regimen includes enalapril, metformin, and atorvastatin. He denies any history of smoking or drinking.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Scabies.

Thank you for that detailed history; the combination of intense itching, red bumps on the thigh, and recent travel to Miami strongly suggests scabies. Given your history of diabetes, I am also concerned about secondary skin infections. Can you confirm if the itching is significantly worse at night and if any household members are experiencing similar symptoms?
